angularDiameterSource: Computed: the volume-equivalent radius of Zhao et al. 2009's polar and equatorial radii at the Hipparcos distance; the paper fits the radii, not a single diameter.
distanceSource: Inverse of the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 66.50 ± 0.11 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) via SIMBAD
radiusSource: Radius: the volume-equivalent sphere of the polar radius 2.162 ± 0.036 and equatorial radius 2.740 ± 0.044 solar radii of Zhao et al. 2009 (https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2241), Table 3, non-standard model (beta free), adopted as the final model; the scene draws the flattening. presentationUp: the measured rotation pole is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 7510 ± 160 K, the true effective temperature of the beta-free model of Zhao et al. 2009 (ApJ 701, 209; https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2241), Table 3.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass 1.92 ± 0.04 solar masses of Zhao et al. 2009 (ApJ 701, 209; https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2241), Table 3, and the volume-equivalent radius, log10(GM/R^2) in cgs

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; the photosphere of a giant star is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp.
